headline: South Asia: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
- Western Russia: Russians hit house with guided bomb in Kharkiv: one killed, 17 injured, including children.
- Asia: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as northern fighting escalates.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Navy awards RTX’s Raytheon $24.4B for SM-6 missiles amid stockpile concerns.
- Military Times, 16 hours ago: US Navy awards RTX’s Raytheon $24.4B for SM-6 missiles amid stockpile concerns.
The deal for the SM-6 interceptors comes as the Pentagon pushes to replenish munitions stockpiles depleted by conflicts in the Middle East.
- Military Times, 21 hours ago: Navy Expeditionary Combat Command rebranded to reflect warfare evolution.
CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle announced that the Navy Expeditionary Combat Command will now be known as Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
- Military Times, one hour ago: Marine Corps plans new warfighter test for future generals.
Following Pentagon guidelines, the Marine Corps is developing and testing its own Joint Warfighter Evaluation.
- Military Times, 20 hours ago: Boeing adds to big week with first full-rate Grey Wolf helicopter order.
The U.S. Air Force awarded Boeing a roughly $85 million contract for four more MH-139A Grey Wolf helicopters, with the first under full-rate production.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Doctors demand timeline for IDT ruling.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Doctors demand timeline for IDT ruling.
The Jamaica Medical Doctors Association (JMDA) is calling for the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to provide a timeline for delivering its ruling in the longstanding dispute between doctors and the Ministry of Health and Wellness over overtime payments. In a press release, JMDA President Jubilee Brown-Service said it took note of the IDT’s September 30 statement, which conceded that “justice delayed is justice denied”. “We call on the IDT to stop denying justice to our doctors by handing down its award without further delay,” the JMDA declared.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 20 hours ago: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
Federico Aramburú, who was killed in March 2022 after a bar brawl, will lend his name to a social commitment award La entrada Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Russians hit house with guided bomb in Kharkiv: one killed, 17 injured, including children.
- Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russians hit house with guided bomb in Kharkiv: one killed, 17 injured, including children.
One person was killed and 17 people, including children, were injured as a result of Russian strikes on two districts of Kharkiv with guided aerial bombs on the afternoon of 2 October. People may still be trapped under the rubble.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: Zelenskyy on Russian strikes on Kyiv: They want Ukrainians to leave the capital.
Zelenskyy says Russia is intensifying attacks on civilian targets to force Ukrainians to leave Kyiv and predicts further escalation ahead of the US midterm elections.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russians strike Mykolaiv: 3 injured, warehouses, offices and hotel damaged.
Three people were injured and port infrastructure, an administrative building, warehouses, offices and a hotel and restaurant site were damaged in Russian strikes on Mykolaiv on 2 October.
- The Moscow Times, 22 hours ago: Putin Says World Is Living Through a Dangerous Moment, Warns West Not to Escalate.
He reiterated that Moscow would resort to all weapons in its arsenal, including nuclear ones, if its Baltic exclave of Kaliningrad was threatened.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions.
- Balkan Insight, 22 hours ago: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions.
Large crowds attend rally in Pristina against Hague court verdict convicting four former Kosovo Liberation Army leaders of war crimes, with protest speaker attacking 'double standards when it comes to justice'.
- Politico Europe, 10 hours ago: How a failed attack in Leipzig revealed a wider Russian campaign.
Documents obtained by the Axel Springer Global Reporters Network trace drone bombs, incendiary parcels and arson attacks to Russian intelligence.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Tories warn Burnham’s EU ‘pandering’ will shred post-Brexit trade deals.
Three former ministers tell POLITICO of “grave consequences” if the U.K. moves closer to the EU under prime minister's bid for a revamped relationship.
- Balkan Insight, 8 hours ago: By Skoda and By Bike: Serbia’s Not Completely Even Election Race.
Crowdfunding, donations and the volunteer spirit are driving Serbia’s cycling students towards the election finish line on October 25 - while Aleksandar Vucic is promoting a ‘man of the people’ image as he tours the country by car.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Hunger increasing in Yemen, record number of people unable to meet food needs, WFP warns.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Hunger increasing in Yemen, record number of people unable to meet food needs, WFP warns.
Yemen is experiencing the most serious escalation between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthi group since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks ​in 2022.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Ukraine calls for tighter sanctions as Russian attacks spark Kyiv gridlock.
Closure of bridges struck by drones in Ukrainian capital causes traffic chaos.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 4 hours ago: New aircraft carrier, 10,000 US troops: Is the Iran war about to escalate?.
By the end of November, three US aircraft carriers and two amphibious landing groups will be positioned near Iran.
- Jerusalem Post, 4 hours ago: Indian flydubai pilot who opened cockpit door shares story with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
According to the wounded pilot, Capt. Smit Machchhar, he had opened the cockpit door while on the floor of the plane and actively being attacked by his Omani copilot.
Africa - bottom line: Nigeria: Troops Rescue 10 Prospective Corps Members Abducted in Imo.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 4 hours ago: Nigeria: Troops Rescue 10 Prospective Corps Members Abducted in Imo.
[Vanguard] Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised 16 terrorists and recovered weapons after repelling simultaneous attacks in Adamawa.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 5 hours ago: Uganda: Uganda to Host Inaugural Conference On Military Operations Other Than War.
[Nile Post] Uganda will next week host the inaugural Conference on Military Operations Other Than War (MOOTW), bringing together military commanders, regional security bodies and peace support mission leaders from across Africa to discuss emerging security threats and non-traditional approaches to conflict management.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 9 hours ago: Sudan: Women's Groups Report Widespread Sexual Violence and Detention Across Sudan.
[Dabanga] Women's rights groups have reported widespread sexual violence, exploitation and detention of women and girls across Sudan, warning that fear, insecurity and restrictions on documentation are masking the scale of abuses.
- Africanews, one hour ago: 'Sad exit': Portugal fans mourn hinted end of Ronaldo era.
Portugal fans are in mourning as Cristiano Ronaldo is seemingly living his last moments with the national team. The star forward walked out of the team’s training camp on Wednesday, hours after coach Jorge Jesus said he would not start Thursday’s Nations League game against Denmark.
South Africa - bottom line: Zimbabwe: Stanbic Bank Zim to Finance Chirundu Border Post Upgrade Project.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Stanbic Bank Zim to Finance Chirundu Border Post Upgrade Project.
[263Chat] The Chirundu Border Post Upgrade and Modernisation Project has reached financial close, marking a major step towards the redevelopment of one of Zimbabwe's key gateways to the region.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 6 hours ago: South Africa: Would Homegrown LEN Cost More? Why SA Should Still Make the HIV Prevention Jab.
[Bhekisisa] South Africa wants to make the six-monthly HIV prevention injection lenacapavir locally. But cheaper generics made elsewhere are expected from 2027. Vinodh Aroon Edward explains why getting the jab to people quickly must come first -- while South Africa builds the skills to make it here.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Chivayo, Wife, Three Others' Heavily Dismembered Bodies Removed From Crash Site After 18-Hour Operation.
[New Zimbabwe] THE heavily dismembered bodies of controversial businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife Lucy Muteke and three others killed in a plane crash were finally removed from the wreckage site about 18 hours after the tragedy.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: Zimbabwe: NPA Goes Pink in Push for Early Breast Cancer Detection.
[263Chat] The National Prosecuting Authority of Zimbabwe (NPAZ) has joined the global campaign to raise awareness about breast cancer, calling on women and communities to prioritise breast health and early detection.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned an attack by the Houthi militia on the Taibah power distribution station in Madina on Sept 29, describing it as a “grave provocation” and a threat to regional peace and security. In a statement, the Foreign Office (FO) said the attack targeted civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Holy Prophet’s (PBUH) Mosque. “The sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances,” the FO said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Trump calls Iran’s Hormuz offer ‘not enough’.
• US president warns strikes against Tehran could resume after midterms; Washington sanctions Iran’s top carmakers, rail operators • Pezeshkian says his country is open to dialogue; Putin hopes the strait reopens, says Russia’s offer to take enriched uranium still stands PRESIDENT Donald Trump rejected Iran’s offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz as “simply not enough”, warning that military action against Tehran could resume after the midterm elections and predicting long-term peace with the country is unlikely.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Army's top brass warns of 'decisive force' against any 'May 9-like situation'.
The army’s top brass on Friday warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”, according to the military’s media wing. The warning came during the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference in Rawalpindi, which was presided over by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.
- The Hindu - International, 22 hours ago: Pakistan says killed 22 terrorists in airstrikes in Afghanistan.
Afghanistan's Taliban government, meanwhile, said that Pakistani strikes killed nine Afghan civilians, including women and children, and injured 11 others.
Asia - bottom line: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as northern fighting escalates.
- South China Morning Post - China, Africanews, 6 hours ago: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as northern fighting escalates.
Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on Thursday, accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts as fighting continued in northern Ethiopia. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing a rebel group, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which launched a major assault against government forces last week, raising fears of a return to the devastating 2020–2022 civil war that killed an estimated 600,000 people. Addis Ababa said it was expelling 10 Eritrean diplomats who “pose a direct...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Ukraine war: Japan’s new sanctions on Russia target oil exports.
The Japanese government on Friday announced additional sanctions against Russia amid the ongoing invasion of Ukraine, targeting a so-called shadow fleet of vessels engaged in transporting sanctioned oil from Russia. Joining international efforts to crack down on sanctions evasion by the fleet, Japan has decided to impose restrictions on the provision of services to 35 vessels, according to the Foreign Ministry. The measures restrict the provision of services including insurance, maritime...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: China’s PLA sets up new military academy colleges for AI, drones and discipline.
China has set up several new institutions at military academies to train specialists in hi-tech and discipline inspection as the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) works towards its centennial modernisation goals. The College of Unmanned and Intelligent Engineering, the College of Combat Support NCOs (Non-Commissioned Officers) and the College of Equipment Support NCOs were established within the PLA Army Engineering University on Wednesday. On the same day, the National Defence University (NDU),...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Indian pilot hailed as hero recalls Flydubai cockpit attack.
The Indian airline captain who helped thwart an apparent attempt to crash a Flydubai flight described on Friday how he fought for his life in the minutes after his co-pilot stabbed him and the plane began a steep descent. Captain Smit Machchhar, recovering in an Abu Dhabi hospital, told Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in a televised video call that he knew he had to get back on his feet to save his passengers. “I had so many wounds. - NDTV - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: 3rd Aircraft Carrier, 10,000 Troops Head To Middle East After Trump's Warning.
The USS Theodore Roosevelt and its strike group carrying the service members would arrive in the Middle East by the end of November. Currently two other aircraft carriers are stationed in the region -- the USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington.

- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: 'Terrorist act': UAE official on flydubai attack, praises India pilot Smit Machchhar.

South Korean Unification Minister Chung Dong-young warned against politicizing the Sept. 21 mine blast in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) that left several soldiers injured and argued the incident should not be used to undermine Seoul’s efforts to pursue peace with North Korea. “Stoking hatred and hostility is not politics,” he told news reporters Friday in […]

Regional Victorian couple who died in a multi-vehicle crash are remembered as "loving" and "caring" people.
